title: Drake Maye, A.J. Brown heat up and other takeaways from Day 6 of Patriots training camp
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Drake Maye excelled in team drills, completing 11 of 11 throws during the 11-on-11s at Patriots' training camp.
A.J. Brown built chemistry with Maye, catching several passes during the second padded practice in training camp.
Rookie tight end Eli Raridon impressed, catching a touchdown during 7-on-7 drills and solidifying his role as backup.

title: Massachusetts falls out of top 10 in best state rankings by U.S. News & World Report
author: Annie Jonas
bullets: Massachusetts drops to No. 11 in U.S. News & World Report's 2026 Best States rankings, down two spots from 2025.
The state maintains strong healthcare positions, ranking second nationally and being a pioneer in universal healthcare legislation.
Massachusetts ranked poorly in fiscal stability (39th) and infrastructure (38th), impacting its overall ranking.

title: Massachusetts loses two IHOP restaurants
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: IHOP has closed its locations in Cambridge and Hyannis, leaving 19 other restaurants open in Massachusetts.
The closures may stem from insufficient foot traffic or expired leases; the Cambridge location often seemed empty.
Owned by Dine Brands Global, IHOP has 1,812 franchised and 12 company-owned restaurants, planning 245 more franchises.

title: Court agrees Wu did not discriminate against North End restaurants, but may have illegally taxed them
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: A federal appeals court dismissed North End restaurants' discrimination lawsuit, siding with Boston Mayor Michelle Wu's administration on outdoor dining regulations.
The court found the complaint of anti-Italian discrimination unsupported, upholding the lower court's rejection of five out of six claims.
The ruling allows North End restaurants to pursue claims that $7,500 impact fees might be an unlawful tax, dismissing it without prejudice.

title: MassDOT releases rendering of two new bridges along McGrath Highway
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: MassDOT plans to replace the Squires Bridge along the Somerville/Cambridge line as part of McGrath Boulevard improvements.
The new Squires Bridge will be a 300-foot beam bridge, while the Somerville Avenue Extension Bridge will reroute 'Scary Way'.
Construction for the bridges is slated to start in 2030, with an anticipated completion within three to four years.

title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ review: Peter Parker grows up in emotionally mature sequel
author: Kevin Slane
bullets: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' stars Tom Holland as a more mature Peter Parker dealing with personal struggles.
The film showcases a darker, gray New York City and emphasizes small-scale storytelling, avoiding multiverse themes.
Zendaya's role as MJ is expanded, highlighting her chemistry with Holland and showcasing her acting range.

title: This Boston law firm is boosting starting salaries to $235,000
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: McDermott Will & Schulte LLP boosts starting salary for first-year associates to $235,000 in Boston.
McDermott aims to stay competitive with top firms as national salaries for young lawyers rise.
Boston law firms like Ropes & Gray, Goodwin, and others have not announced matching salary increases.

title: Boston will host the second-ever National Urban Rat Summit
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Boston will host the National Urban Rat Summit on September 23-24, announced by Mayor Michelle Wu.
The summit follows Boston's proactive rodent control approach, reducing reliance on dangerous rodenticides.
New data reveal Boston rats spread leptospirosis, highlighting urgency in advancing pest control strategies.

title: Mass. postal worker robbed at gunpoint
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Billerica Police are investigating an armed robbery where an arrow key was stolen from a USPS employee.
The robbery took place outside a Postal Service facility at 5 Brick Kiln Road at 4:25 p.m. Thursday.
The suspects, in a black Cadillac, fled towards Chelmsford Street after displaying a handgun.

title: Myrtle the sea turtle weighs nearly 500 pounds. What does it take to keep her healthy?
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Myrtle, a green sea turtle at the New England Aquarium, weighs 488 pounds and undergoes quarterly health check-ups.
Veterinary staff conduct blood tests, ultrasounds, and check turtles' flippers and shells during annual exams at the aquarium.
Data from captive turtles like Myrtle inform rehabilitation efforts for Massachusetts' cold-stunned sea turtles at the Quincy facility.
